title: Agent Toolkit Baseline Profile
description: The canonical set of characteristics every agent in the toolkit inherits from. Lives at ~/.agent-toolkit/baseline.yaml.

x-composite-questions.label: Risk posture
x-composite-questions.question: How much should agents be allowed to do unsupervised?
x-composite-questions.help: One answer sets both the capability set and the guardrails. Web search is granted at every posture and page fetching at all but the strictest — withholding read-only network access is a worse failure than the risk it avoids (D12). Full mode walks those two characteristics field by field instead.

answers.label: Cautious
answers.help: Read-only filesystem and web search, every output checked, a human in the loop.

answers.label: Balanced
answers.help: Write within the workspace, search and fetch the web, no human gate. The default.

answers.label: Autonomous
answers.help: Everything above plus shell and subagents, with no tool-use ceiling.

schema_version.description: Schema version. Bumped when fields are added, renamed, or removed; drives migration.

locale.x-help: Language, region, and date/number/currency formatting conventions

domain.x-question: What industry or subject area will your agents mostly work in?
domain.x-help: Industry or subject area the agent will operate from

audience.x-question: Who is the output usually for?
audience.x-help: Who the agent's output is for (internal team, external client, technical vs non-technical)

tone_of_voice.x-question: How should agents write by default?

persona.x-question: Should agents have a named persona, or stay neutral?
persona.x-help: Whether the agent has a name/character, or stays neutral/utilitarian

verbosity.x-question: How much should agents write by default?
verbosity.x-help: Default output length/density (concise bullets vs full prose)

formatting_conventions.x-question: What house style should agents use for markdown?
formatting_conventions.x-help: House style for markdown headers, tables, code blocks, etc.

model.description: Default model. Mid-tier by design — agents override up only when needed.
model.x-question: Which model should agents use by default?
model.x-help: Default LLM model to utilise — baseline is a mid-tier model (e.g. Sonnet) to avoid cost blowouts from defaulting every agent to the highest-tier model; agents can override up where a task genuinely needs it

pattern.x-question: Which agent pattern should be the default?
pattern.x-help: Default agent pattern from a small enumerated set (not free text) — baseline is `standalone`; other values to introduce as needed: `pipeline`, `router`, `parallel`, `orchestrator-workers` (aka hierarchical-supervisory), `evaluator-optimizer`, `collaborative` (aka peer-to-peer/swarm). Keep the default simple; expand the set only when a real use case needs it

guardrails.x-question: Which guardrails should apply by default?
guardrails.x-help: Input filtering, tool-use limits, and output validation to apply — recurs as its own concern across every pattern, separate from the pattern itself. In Express mode this is asked as a single "risk posture" question

evaluation_loop.x-question: Should agents self-review before returning output?
evaluation_loop.x-help: Whether the agent self-reviews or is checked by a second pass before returning output (off by default for a standalone agent; on for patterns like evaluator-optimizer)

permissions_scope.x-question: What should agents be allowed to touch?
permissions_scope.x-help: What the agent is and isn't allowed to touch, as a closed capability vocabulary (`file.read`, `file.search`, `file.write`, `shell`, `web.search`, `web.fetch`, `subagent`) plus the domain lists that bound `web.fetch` — also covered by the risk posture question

capabilities.description: Closed vocabulary. Replaces v1's `tools`, whose names mapped to no runtime, and v1's `external_calls`, which conflated web search, page fetching and arbitrary egress into one boolean. REPLACES the inherited list; never appends.

web.description: Parameters for web.fetch only. Granting or withholding web access is the capability's job; these bound where it may go.

safety_compliance_profile.x-question: Any regulatory or org-specific compliance profile to inherit?
safety_compliance_profile.x-help: Regulatory or org-specific guardrails to inherit

cost_performance_budget.x-question: What token and latency budget should agents assume?
cost_performance_budget.x-help: Token limits, preferred model tier, latency tolerance

default_context_sources.x-question: Which skills or docs should agents load on init?
default_context_sources.x-help: Which skills/docs/knowledge base the agent should pull from on init
default_context_sources.description: Paths an agent loads on start, relative to its own directory. Empty by default: reusable guidance belongs in library/ and is composed, not loaded by path.

memory_behaviour.x-question: Should agents persist state across runs, or start fresh?
memory_behaviour.x-help: Whether it persists state across runs or starts fresh each time

context_management.x-question: How should agents keep the context window under control?
context_management.x-help: How the agent keeps its context window under control as a run grows — default truncation/pagination limits on tool output, and whether stale tool calls/results get cleared as token limits approach

output_format_contract.x-question: What output format should agents produce by default?
output_format_contract.x-help: Markdown by default, for human consumption; JSON or another machine-readable format only where a downstream agent/tool specifically needs it

output_location.x-question: Where should agent results be written?
output_location.x-help: Default output directory (e.g. `./output`) that agent results are written to, rather than the project root

escalation_path.x-question: What should an agent hand off to when it hits its limits?
escalation_path.x-help: Who/what it hands off to when it hits its limits (another agent, a human)

feedback_mode.x-question: How do you want to give agents feedback?
feedback_mode.x-help: Supports both live chat-based feedback and bulk written feedback — a steering/notes file the agent reads and applies on request, for guidance considered offline and brought back later rather than given turn-by-turn in chat

credentials.description: Environment variable REFERENCES only. Never literal secret values.
credentials.x-question: Which credentials will agents need, by environment variable name?
credentials.x-help: Environment variable *names* only, never values. Validation rejects any literal secret. See [`docs/environment-variables.md`](../../docs/environment-variables.md)

extends.description: Path to a parent profile. Null/absent on the baseline itself; set on agent override files.

compose.description: Library modules to inline into this agent's generated CLAUDE.md, as kind/name. Roles and routines only: a pattern is named by operating_constraints.pattern, and two ways to say the same thing is two ways to disagree. REPLACES the inherited list; never appends.
compose.x-question: Which library modules should every agent compose by default?
compose.x-help: Reusable behaviour inlined into each agent's generated `CLAUDE.md` — roles and routines from `library/`. Most baselines compose nothing and let each agent choose; see `library/README.md`
